These items are intentionally out of scope for the deterministic imaging parity program but should not be forgotten once the required workshop-complete imaging matrix is green.

issues.title: Implement CASA cubic spectral interpolation parity
issues.body:
## Summary
Wave 3 closed with source-backed spectral-seam parity for the pinned gate cases, but `cubic` interpolation is still unimplemented.

The CLI/frontend previously accepted `--interpolation cubic` while silently executing linear behavior. That has now been tightened so `cubic` is rejected explicitly until the real CASA-compatible behavior exists.

## Why this matters
`cubic` belongs to the spectral preparation seam, not a later dirty/gridding stage. It should produce source-channel contribution weights and prepared samples that match CASA/casacore behavior on pinned cube/cubedata oracle cases.

## Required work
- implement CASA-compatible cubic spectral interpolation in the Wave 3 prepared-visibility seam
- emit the resulting cubic contribution coefficients in the oracle trace bundle
- add source-backed CASA oracle coverage for at least one pinned `cube` case and one `cubedata` case that explicitly request cubic interpolation
- keep rejecting unsupported modes only until the implementation is real; do not silently alias cubic to linear

## Notes
Current behavior is intentionally strict:
- `nearest` and `linear` are supported
- `cubic` is rejected as not implemented

issues.title: Close CASA per-channel Briggs cube weighting parity gaps
issues.body:
## Summary
The deterministic Wave 7 weighting/normalization gates are green, but an additional cubedata Briggs stress case still shows a Rust/CASA dirty-image mismatch on `refim_Cband.G37line.ms`.

This is not the same problem as the earlier Wave 7 harness bug in `cube_channel_spw_selector()`. The Rust and CASA parity runners now agree on:
- explicit `spw` channel ranges
- `interpolation='linear'`
- `specmode='cubedata'`
- `perchanweightdensity=true`

The mismatch persists after those harness fixes, so the remaining gap appears to be a real cubedata-specific weighted imaging discrepancy.

## Reproduction
From branch `imaging-improvements` with test data mounted at `/Volumes/home/casatestdata`:

```bash
CASA_RS_TESTDATA_ROOT=/Volumes/home/casatestdata \
  cargo test -p casars-imager --features slow-tests --test imager_casa_parity \
  dirty_cubedata_briggs_products_track_casa_on_refim_cband_g37line -- --exact --nocapture
```

## Current failure
The failing assertion is the center pixel of the dirty image at `[128,128,18]`:
- Rust: `95.01736`
- CASA: `92.63`
- delta: `2.3873596`
- limit: `1.9003471`

Representative panic:

```text
thread 'dirty_cubedata_briggs_products_track_casa_on_refim_cband_g37line' panicked at crates/casars-imager/tests/imager_casa_parity.rs:8494:5:
Rust cubedata briggs image[128,128,18] mismatch: left=95.01736, right=92.63, delta=2.3873596, limit=1.9003471
```

## Nearby evidence
The following related cases are green on the same branch:
- `dirty_cubedata_products_track_casa_on_refim_cband_g37line`
- `dirty_cube_products_track_casa_on_refim_cband_g37line`
- `cube_perchanweight_briggs_tracks_casa_on_refim_point_withline`
- `uniform_dirty_products_track_casa_headers_and_pixels`
- `briggs_dirty_products_track_casa_headers_and_pixels`
- `m51_briggs_dirty_products_track_casa_headers_and_pixels`

That narrows the residual gap to cubedata-specific weighted dirty behavior rather than the generic Briggs weighting seam.

## Suggested next investigation
1. Compare the prepared cubedata per-channel sample traces for this case against CASA, especially the exact source-channel contribution maps and interpolation coefficients near the selected spectral window.
2. Compare per-plane weight-density inputs and normalization states for the Rust and CASA cubedata runs.
3. Confirm whether cubedata Briggs in CASA is sensitive to additional source-channel support beyond the selected output range in a way we are still not mirroring exactly.

issues.title: [Imaging] Complete remaining CASA tclean selectdata selectors
issues.body:
Audit source:
- CASA tclean docs: https://casadocs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/tt/casatasks.imaging.tclean.html
- Local parity audit against `casars-imager` and `casa-imaging`

Problem
The current frontend accepts only a subset of CASA tclean's input and `selectdata` surface.

CASA documents support for:
- multiple input MSs (`vis` as a list)
- `timerange`
- `uvrange`
- `antenna`
- `scan`
- `observation`
- `intent`

The current Rust frontend is much narrower: one `--ms`, plus field/SPW/DDID/channel/datacolumn-style selection. That means a major part of common real-world tclean selection workflows still cannot even be expressed, regardless of what the lower-level imaging kernels can do.

Scope
- Extend the public imaging frontend and internal orchestration to support:
  - multiple input MeasurementSets
  - the missing selectdata selectors listed above
- Preserve deterministic seam tracing across the expanded selection surface.
- Define stable row-order/selection-oracle artifacts for multi-MS runs.
- Add parity gates that prove row selection identity before any image-level comparison.

Suggested gates
- one multi-MS continuum imaging selection gate
- one selector-heavy gate that uses at least `timerange` + `scan` or `intent`
- seam-level proof that the selected row ids/order match CASA on the same selection request

issues.title: [Imaging] Complete the remaining CASA tclean spectral/moving-source surface (cubesource, mvc, TRACKFIELD)
issues.body:
Audit source:
- CASA tclean docs: https://casadocs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/tt/casatasks.imaging.tclean.html
- Local parity audit against `casars-imager` and `casa-imaging`

Problem
The current spectral/moving-source surface still trails CASA tclean in several major ways.

CASA documents:
- `specmode=cubesource`
- `specmode=mvc`
- moving-source tracking via `phasecenter='TRACKFIELD'` and named/ephemeris phase centers
- cubic spectral interpolation

Rust currently supports only `mfs`, `cube`, and `cubedata` in the public surface, explicitly rejects cubic interpolation today, and blocks explicit `--phasecenter` for cube-like imaging.

Scope
- Add the missing major spectral/moving-source modes:
  - `cubesource`
  - `mvc`
  - moving-source / ephemeris-aware tracking semantics equivalent to CASA's `TRACKFIELD` path where required by pinned datasets
- Expand cube-like phase-center handling so the public surface can express the same major requests that CASA can.
- Keep the prepared spectral seam explicit: source-channel indices, interpolation coefficients, frame conversion, and tracking metadata must remain oracle-visible.

Relationship to existing work
- Cubic interpolation is already tracked in #42 and should not be duplicated here.
- This issue covers the rest of the missing documented spectral/moving-source tclean surface, and should coordinate with #42 rather than replace it.

Suggested gates
- one `cubesource` or equivalent source-frame spectral gate
- one moving-source / tracked-field gate using a pinned ephemeris-capable dataset
- seam-level proof of tracking/reprojection behavior before end-product parity

issues.title: Automasking parity: add standard-gridder PB product and product pixel masks
issues.body:
## Outcome

Add CASA-compatible primary-beam product and image pixel-mask behavior for standard-gridder cube tutorial runs, so tutorial parity comparisons do not rely on CASA-only PB/product validity masks.

## Parent context

- Follow-up from Wave 6B issue #167 and PR #213.
- Tutorial route: `alma/automasking` / Automasking Guide.
- Observed during same-input CASA C++ vs casa-rs review of `twhya_base_params`.

## Current evidence

The #167 same-input run shows the CLEAN `.mask` product itself is close, but CASA C++ also emits and attaches a primary-beam/product pixel mask that casa-rs does not currently reproduce in the standard-gridder cube path.

Observed artifacts:

- CASA C++ wrote `twhya_base_params.pb`; casa-rs did not write a `.pb` product for this standard-gridder cube run.
- CASA C++ attached a product pixel mask to `.image` / `.residual`; casa-rs wrote those products as fully valid.
- CASA `.image` / `.residual` valid pixels: `643,935 / 937,500`.
- casa-rs `.image` / `.residual` valid pixels: `937,500 / 937,500`.
- CASA and casa-rs CLEAN `.mask` products are both fully valid; the automask mask pixels are a separate comparison surface.

This means #167 has automask-mask parity evidence, but not complete tutorial-visible product parity for PB/product masks.

## Scope

- Inspect CASA C++ / task behavior for standard-gridder cube `.pb` product generation and product pixel-mask attachment.
- Implement the corresponding casa-rs standard-gridder cube `.pb` product and image/residual pixel-mask behavior required by tutorial-visible products.
- Ensure comparison tooling reports PB/product mask parity separately from CLEAN `.mask` parity.
- Update the Automasking Guide parity evidence to include side-by-side CASA C++ / casa-rs / difference panels or equivalent metrics for the PB mask/product validity surface.

## Non-goals

- Do not broaden this into full mosaic primary-beam parity unless CASA source inspection shows the same code path is required for the standard-gridder tutorial product.
- Do not change the already implemented auto-multithresh mask algorithm unless PB/product-mask semantics affect the CLEAN mask itself.

## Acceptance checks

- [ ] Source-backed notes identify the CASA C++/task code path that produces `.pb` and attaches product pixel masks for the relevant standard-gridder cube products.
- [ ] casa-rs writes the tutorial-visible `.pb` product for the same standard-gridder cube run where CASA C++ writes it.
- [ ] casa-rs `.image` and `.residual` validity masks match CASA C++ for the Automasking Guide same-input run, or any accepted difference is explicitly documented with impact.
- [ ] Numeric parity report includes product valid-pixel counts and mismatch counts for `.image`, `.residual`, `.mask`, and `.pb`.
- [ ] Inspectable panels show CASA C++, casa-rs, and difference views for the PB/product-mask surface.
- [ ] #167 / PR #213 closeout or follow-up notes link this issue as the deferred tutorial-visible PB/product-mask parity gap.

## Stop conditions

- Stop before changing persisted image/table format semantics without explicit review.
- Stop and split if CASA source inspection shows this requires a broad primary-beam model or mosaic-gridder redesign beyond standard-gridder tutorial products.
